stem: Which choice best states the main idea of the text?
passage: Researchers at the University of Helsinki recently completed a seven-year study tracking the foraging patterns of Eurasian jays in fragmented boreal forests. The team fitted 143 birds with lightweight GPS transmitters and recorded over 2.6 million location points. Their findings indicate that jays in highly fragmented landscapes travel, on average, 37 percent farther per day than jays in continuous forest to acquire comparable quantities of food. The additional energy expenditure, the researchers note, may reduce overwinter survival rates by as much as 11 percent, underscoring the hidden metabolic costs that habitat fragmentation imposes on scatter-hoarding species.

options.text: Habitat fragmentation forces Eurasian jays to travel significantly farther for food, which may lower their survival rates.
GPS transmitter technology has enabled researchers to collect unprecedented amounts of data on bird movement patterns.
Eurasian jays are better adapted to continuous forests than to fragmented landscapes because they cache food in scattered locations.
A seven-year study in Finland found that boreal forests are declining at a faster rate than scientists had previously estimated.

explanation: The passage centers on the finding that jays in fragmented forests must travel 37 percent farther for food and that this extra energy expenditure may reduce their overwinter survival. The choice stating that habitat fragmentation forces jays to travel farther and may lower survival rates captures this central point. The choice about GPS technology describes only the study's methodology, not its central finding. The choice about jays being better adapted to continuous forests introduces a comparative claim the passage never makes. The choice about boreal forest decline rates misrepresents the study's subject entirely, since the passage discusses jay foraging costs, not deforestation rates.

stem: Which choice best states the main idea of the text?
passage: In 1928, the Indian physicist C. V. Raman demonstrated that when monochromatic light passes through a transparent substance, a small fraction of the scattered light emerges at wavelengths different from the incident beam. This phenomenon, now called the Raman effect, occurs because photons exchange energy with molecular vibrations, shifting to either higher or lower frequencies. Although the effect is extremely weak -- typically only one in ten million photons is Raman-scattered -- modern laser sources and sensitive detectors have turned Raman spectroscopy into a workhorse analytical technique. Today it is used to identify pharmaceutical compounds, authenticate gemstones, detect explosives at airport checkpoints, and even analyze the pigments in centuries-old paintings without damaging them.

options.text: An obscure quantum phenomenon discovered in the early twentieth century has become the basis for a versatile and widely applied analytical technique.
C. V. Raman's discovery of inelastic light scattering earned him immediate recognition but had no practical applications until laser technology matured decades later.
Raman spectroscopy is superior to all other methods of chemical analysis because it can identify substances without physical contact.
The weakness of the Raman effect has limited its usefulness primarily to high-budget research laboratories with specialized equipment.

explanation: The passage traces the Raman effect from its 1928 discovery through its development into a widely used analytical tool, making the choice about an obscure phenomenon becoming a versatile technique the best summary of the central idea. The choice claiming Raman received immediate recognition and that the technique had no applications until lasers arrived overstates what the passage says -- the text never discusses Raman's recognition or claims there were zero earlier uses. The choice asserting superiority over all other methods introduces a superlative comparison absent from the passage. The choice about limited usefulness directly contradicts the passage's emphasis on the technique's broad modern applications.

stem: Which choice best states the main idea of the text?
passage: Conventional accounts of the Harlem Renaissance emphasize its literary and musical achievements while treating the visual arts as secondary. Art historian Bridget R. Cooks challenges this narrative, arguing that painters such as Aaron Douglas and sculptors such as Augusta Savage were not merely illustrating ideas generated by writers but were independently theorizing Black modernity through form and material. Douglas's layered silhouettes, for instance, drew on Egyptian wall painting and Art Deco geometry to propose a visual genealogy linking African diasporic peoples across centuries -- a historiographic argument that had no direct parallel in the contemporaneous poetry of Langston Hughes or Claude McKay. By foregrounding the conceptual autonomy of these visual artists, Cooks contends, scholars can recover a dimension of the Renaissance that literary-centered histories have systematically obscured.

options.text: Bridget R. Cooks argues that Harlem Renaissance visual artists were independent theorists of Black modernity whose contributions have been undervalued by literary-focused histories.
Aaron Douglas's use of Egyptian and Art Deco visual elements was more innovative than the literary techniques employed by Langston Hughes and Claude McKay.
The Harlem Renaissance is best understood as a movement in which writers and visual artists collaborated closely to advance a shared political agenda.
Art historians have recently discovered previously unknown paintings by Augusta Savage that fundamentally alter scholarly understanding of the Harlem Renaissance.

explanation: The passage presents Cooks's argument that Harlem Renaissance visual artists independently theorized Black modernity and that literary-centered accounts have obscured their conceptual contributions. The choice capturing Cooks's claim about visual artists as independent theorists whose work has been undervalued reflects this central idea. The choice about Douglas being more innovative than Hughes and McKay introduces a qualitative ranking the passage does not make; the text notes Douglas's work had no direct parallel in their poetry, but it does not claim superiority. The choice about close collaboration contradicts the passage's emphasis on the conceptual autonomy of visual artists from writers. The choice about recently discovered paintings fabricates an event the passage never mentions.

stem: A student claims that the drought of 1934 caused more widespread agricultural damage across the United States than any other single-year drought in the twentieth century. Which finding, if true, would most directly support this claim?
passage: Between 1930 and 1940, the Great Plains experienced a series of severe droughts that devastated agricultural output and displaced hundreds of thousands of farming families. The drought conditions were driven by a combination of below-average rainfall, high temperatures, and decades of aggressive plowing that had stripped the topsoil of its natural grass cover. Government meteorologists noted that 1934 and 1936 were the two most acute drought years during this period, though they differed considerably in geographic scope and intensity.

options.text: USDA records show that in 1934, crop failures were reported in 75 percent of U.S. counties, a proportion unmatched by any other single-year drought before or after during the century.
Farmers in the southern Great Plains reported that dust storms in 1935 were more frequent and more damaging than those in any prior year.
The 1936 drought produced the highest recorded temperatures in eleven Midwestern states, breaking records that had stood since the 1890s.
Federal relief spending on drought assistance increased steadily throughout the 1930s, reaching its peak in 1938.

explanation: The claim is specifically that the 1934 drought caused more widespread agricultural damage than any other single-year drought in the twentieth century. The finding about USDA records showing crop failures in 75 percent of counties in 1934, unmatched by any other single-year drought, directly supports both the year and the superlative scope of the claim. The finding about 1935 dust storms concerns a different year and addresses dust storms rather than drought-caused agricultural damage. The finding about 1936 temperatures supports the severity of 1936, not 1934, and addresses heat records rather than agricultural damage. The finding about peak relief spending in 1938 is about federal expenditure trends, not the geographic breadth of agricultural damage in any single drought year.

stem: A marine biologist hypothesizes that deep-sea bioluminescent organisms use distinct flash patterns primarily to coordinate schooling behavior rather than to attract prey. Which finding, if true, would most directly weaken this hypothesis?
passage: Many deep-sea fish and invertebrates produce light through chemical reactions involving the enzyme luciferase. Scientists have long debated the primary function of bioluminescence in these organisms. Proposed functions include attracting prey, deterring predators through startle displays, facilitating mate recognition, and coordinating group movement in lightless environments. Recent advances in submersible camera technology have enabled researchers to observe bioluminescent behaviors in situ at depths exceeding 3,000 meters for the first time.

options.text: High-speed video analysis reveals that 89 percent of observed flash sequences in the anglerfish Cryptopsaras couesii occur when the fish is solitary and stationary, ceasing immediately when small crustaceans approach the lure.
Laboratory experiments show that certain bioluminescent jellyfish increase their flash rate when exposed to simulated predator shadows.
Genetic sequencing indicates that the luciferase gene evolved independently at least 47 times across marine lineages.
Population surveys find that bioluminescent species are more abundant in the mesopelagic zone than in the bathypelagic zone.

explanation: The hypothesis claims that bioluminescent flashing serves primarily to coordinate schooling. The finding that 89 percent of flash sequences occur when anglerfish are solitary and stationary -- and stop when prey approach the lure -- directly weakens this claim by showing the dominant use is solitary and prey-related, not group coordination. The finding about jellyfish increasing flash rates near predator shadows addresses predator deterrence in a different taxon and does not address schooling coordination. The finding about independent evolution of luciferase concerns evolutionary history rather than the behavioral function of flashing. The finding about species abundance across depth zones describes distribution patterns without bearing on whether flashing coordinates schooling.

stem: A political scientist argues that ranked-choice voting (RCV) reduces negative campaigning because candidates must appeal to opponents' supporters for second-choice votes. Which finding, if true, would most directly undermine this argument?
passage: Ranked-choice voting allows voters to rank candidates in order of preference. If no candidate receives a majority of first-choice votes, the candidate with the fewest first-choice votes is eliminated and that candidate's ballots are redistributed according to the voters' next preferences. This process continues until one candidate achieves a majority. Proponents argue that RCV encourages more civil campaigns, reduces strategic voting, and produces winners with broader coalitions of support. Critics counter that RCV introduces ballot complexity, increases rates of ballot exhaustion, and may not deliver the behavioral incentives its advocates claim.

options.text: A study of 97 RCV elections in four U.S. cities finds that candidates' rates of personal attacks, as measured by independent ad-tracking databases, were statistically indistinguishable from rates in comparable plurality elections in matched cities during the same period.
Surveys conducted after RCV elections show that 62 percent of voters found the ranked ballot easy to complete.
In three of the four cities studied, voter turnout in RCV elections was 4 to 7 percentage points higher than in prior plurality elections.
Campaign finance records reveal that candidates in RCV elections spent an average of 14 percent less on advertising than candidates in plurality elections in the same jurisdictions.

explanation: The argument is that RCV reduces negative campaigning. The finding that personal attack rates in 97 RCV elections were statistically indistinguishable from those in comparable plurality elections directly undermines this claim by showing no measurable reduction in negativity. The finding about voters finding ranked ballots easy to complete addresses ballot usability, not campaign tone. The finding about higher voter turnout concerns participation rates, which is a different dimension from campaign negativity. The finding about lower advertising spending addresses total expenditure, not the content or tone of campaigns.

stem: Which choice most logically completes the text?
passage: The fruit fly Drosophila melanogaster has been used in genetics research for over a century, in part because of its rapid generation time: a new generation can be produced every ten to twelve days under laboratory conditions. This speed allows researchers to observe the effects of genetic mutations across many generations in a relatively short period. By contrast, studying comparable multigenerational genetic effects in organisms with longer generation times, such as elephants, which have a gestation period of approximately 22 months, would ________

options.text: require decades of observation, making such studies impractical for most research timelines.
yield more reliable data because larger organisms have more stable genomes.
be unnecessary because elephant genetics are already fully understood.
produce results identical to those obtained from Drosophila studies.

explanation: The passage establishes that Drosophila's value lies in its rapid generation time, which enables multigenerational observation over short periods. The text then contrasts this with elephants' 22-month gestation. The logical completion is that studying comparable multigenerational effects in elephants would require decades, making such research impractical. The choice about more reliable data from larger organisms introduces an unsupported claim about genome stability that the passage does not imply. The choice about elephant genetics being fully understood is contradicted by the passage's framing, which discusses the difficulty of studying such organisms, not the completeness of existing knowledge. The choice about identical results ignores the passage's emphasis on the practical differences between the two organisms.

stem: Which choice most logically completes the text?
passage: During the late nineteenth century, the Chilean government financed the construction of an extensive railway network connecting the nitrate mining regions of the Atacama Desert to Pacific coastal ports. The railways drastically reduced the cost of transporting sodium nitrate, which was then the world's most important agricultural fertilizer, to international markets. By the 1920s, however, German chemist Fritz Haber's process for synthesizing ammonia from atmospheric nitrogen had enabled the industrial production of synthetic fertilizers at a fraction of the cost of natural nitrate. As synthetic fertilizers captured an ever-larger share of the global market, the economic rationale for maintaining the Atacama rail network ________

options.text: eroded, since the mines that the railways had been built to serve were losing their primary customer base to a cheaper substitute product.
strengthened, because the railways could easily be repurposed to transport synthetic fertilizers manufactured in coastal factories.
remained unchanged, as Chilean nitrate continued to dominate global fertilizer markets throughout the twentieth century.
shifted from commercial freight to passenger service as urban populations in the Atacama region expanded rapidly.

explanation: The passage establishes that the railways existed to transport natural nitrate from mines to ports, and that synthetic fertilizers undercut the market for natural nitrate. The logical inference is that as demand for natural nitrate fell, the economic justification for maintaining railways built specifically to serve those mines would erode. The choice about repurposing railways for synthetic fertilizer transport introduces an unsupported scenario the passage gives no basis for -- synthetic fertilizers are described as produced industrially, not in coastal Chilean factories. The choice about continued dominance of Chilean nitrate directly contradicts the passage's statement that synthetic fertilizers were capturing an ever-larger market share. The choice about passenger service and urban expansion introduces facts about population growth that the passage neither states nor implies.

stem: Which choice most logically completes the text?
passage: Neuroscientist Maria Velasco and her team studied how bilingual speakers of Basque and Spanish process grammatically gendered nouns. In Spanish, the word for "bridge" (puente) is masculine, while in Basque, nouns carry no grammatical gender. Velasco found that when bilingual participants were asked to describe bridges in Spanish, they disproportionately used adjectives culturally associated with masculinity, such as "strong" and "imposing." When the same participants described bridges in Basque, no such pattern emerged. Velasco argues that these results complicate the universalist position that conceptual categories are independent of linguistic structure, because if concepts were truly language-independent, ________

options.text: the adjective choices made by the same speakers should have remained consistent regardless of which language they were using at the time of the task.
Basque speakers would have been unable to learn the grammatical gender system of Spanish as adult second-language learners.
Spanish speakers would have applied masculine adjectives to all nouns, not just those with masculine grammatical gender.
the bilingual participants would have preferred Basque over Spanish when asked to describe objects with no clear gender association.

explanation: The universalist position holds that conceptual categories are independent of language. If that were true, the same speakers describing the same object should produce similar adjective patterns regardless of which language they use, since the underlying concept would be stable. The finding that adjective choices shifted depending on the language directly challenges this prediction, which is why consistent adjective choices across languages is the logical completion. The choice about Basque speakers being unable to learn Spanish gender confuses conceptual influence with learnability -- the universalist position concerns whether language shapes thought, not whether grammar systems can be acquired. The choice about Spanish speakers applying masculine adjectives to all nouns mischaracterizes the universalist prediction; the claim is about language-independence of concepts, not about overgeneralization of gender to all nouns. The choice about preferring Basque for gender-neutral objects introduces a language-preference claim that has no basis in the passage's experimental design or the universalist position.
